md_description: This workflow starts with soil samples collected from multiple agricultural fields at different geographic locations and times. The samples are characterized by environmental measurements including pH, moisture, and temperature, then transformed through nucleic acid extraction into sequencing-ready material. Sequencing generates raw metagenomic reads that are processed into community-profile derivatives for downstream analysis of microbial diversity, composition, and environmental associations across seasonal and spatial gradients.

soil_sample.reasoning: For the soil_sample Entity node, I included only intrinsic identity/origin fields that describe what the specimen is and where/when it was collected. I excluded downstream measurement fields such as pH, moisture, and temperature because those belong to separate Capture/Signal nodes already present in the DAG. I also excluded extraction, library prep, sequencing, and analysis details because those are owned by downstream Process/Capture/Derivative nodes. No already_generated fields were provided, so there were no preexisting naming conflicts to avoid. The resulting schema focuses on sample identity, agricultural origin, geographic collection context, collection timing, and basic provenance needed to distinguish specimens across sites and seasons.

md_schema.descr: Unique identifier for the soil specimen in the metadata table; use a stable string such as SAMPLE_0001 or FIELD12_2024_07_15. Assigned at collection and used to link the specimen to all downstream measurements and omics outputs.
Date the soil specimen was collected from the field, recorded at the time of sampling in YYYY-MM-DD format. Use to capture seasonal variation across collection rounds.
Clock time of sampling, recorded at the field collection point in 24-hour HH:MM format when available. Useful for distinguishing multiple samples collected on the same date.
Country where the soil specimen was collected, recorded from the field location at sampling time. Use a standardized geographic name or code such as USA or Kenya.
Subnational geographic region of collection, such as state, province, or district, recorded at sampling time. This supports spatial stratification across agricultural locations.
Human-readable name of the agricultural field, farm, or plot where the specimen was collected. Record the site label used by the study, such as North Farm Plot A.
Sampling location latitude in decimal degrees, recorded at the collection site using GPS or field mapping tools. Typical range is -90 to 90.
Sampling location longitude in decimal degrees, recorded at the collection site using GPS or field mapping tools. Typical range is -180 to 180.
Agricultural context of the sampled field, describing the dominant crop or land-use setting at the time of collection, such as maize field, wheat field, orchard, or fallow plot.
Depth interval from which the soil specimen was collected, measured in centimeters at the time of sampling. Use a single depth or range such as 0-10 cm to describe the sampled horizon.

Season or sampling campaign used to contextualize temporal variation in the study, assigned from the collection date or field campaign design. Example values include spring, summer, autumn, and winter.
Replicate label for the soil specimen when multiple samples were collected from the same site and time point. Use a short string such as R1, R2, or biological_replicate_03.

soil_ph_capture.reasoning: For the soil_ph_capture Capture node, I included only instrument/session configuration fields and excluded the pH result itself because that belongs on the downstream soil_ph_signal node. I also excluded sample identity and collection context because those are owned by the upstream soil_sample Entity node, and I avoided extraction/sequencing/analysis territory because those are downstream processes. Since no already_generated fields were provided in this turn, there were no prior field-name conflicts to resolve. The schema focuses on the configured measurement device and how the pH capture was performed so downstream users can interpret the session and reproduce the measurement.

md_schema.descr: Manufacturer of the field pH meter used to measure soil pH at the sampling site or during the field measurement session. Record the hardware brand name as a string, for example Hanna Instruments or Thermo Fisher Scientific.
Model name or number of the pH meter used for the soil pH capture session. Record the exact instrument model as configured during measurement, for example HI98121 or Orion Star A211.
Serial number of the pH meter used in the capture session, recorded from the instrument label or device record. Use a stable string identifier such as SN1234567 to trace the exact hardware unit.

Operational method used to capture soil pH on the instrument at the time of measurement, such as direct probe insertion, soil-water slurry, or buffered slurry protocol. Choose the method actually used in this experiment.

Temperature of the measurement environment or sample at the time pH was read, if the instrument or protocol records temperature compensation. Record in degrees Celsius, typically within the range of field ambient temperatures.
Calibration standard set used immediately before or during the pH measurement session, such as pH 4.00/7.00/10.00 buffers. Record the standard combination used to verify instrument accuracy.
Date on which the soil pH measurement was performed, recorded at the capture session in YYYY-MM-DD format. Use this to distinguish repeated measurements across field visits.
Clock time when the soil pH measurement was performed, recorded in 24-hour HH:MM format. Useful when multiple measurements are taken on the same day.
Person or field crew member who performed the soil pH measurement. Record as a string identifier or name, for example technician_01, to document the measurement session.

soil_ph_signal.reasoning: For the soil_ph_signal Signal node, I included only raw data artefact fields that describe the pH readout itself: the numeric value, unit/scale, file or record representation if stored digitally, and basic technical quality indicators. I excluded instrument make/model, calibration, and capture-time configuration because those belong to the upstream soil_ph_capture node. I also excluded the soil identity and collection context because those belong to the soil_sample Entity node. No already_generated fields were provided here, so there were no duplicate-name constraints beyond staying within the Signal semantic layer. The schema is intentionally limited to the recorded pH value and its technical representation so downstream users can interpret or archive the measurement without conflating it with capture settings.

md_schema.descr: Recorded soil pH readout for the sample, captured as the raw numeric signal from the pH measurement session. Typical values range from about 3.0 to 10.0 in agricultural soils, depending on soil chemistry and management.

Calibration scale or reference basis used for the reported pH readout, such as water-based or CaCl2-based reporting if applicable in this study. Record the exact reporting basis used for the signal value.
Textual representation of the pH signal as stored in the metadata record or raw output table, such as 6.7 or 7.15. Useful when the original readout is preserved as a string in exported files.

Quality flag for the recorded pH readout indicating whether the signal was accepted for downstream use, corrected, or rejected due to instrument or handling issues. Assign at the time the raw readout is stored.

Storage location or file reference for the raw pH readout if it is written to a digital instrument log or data table. Use a path, filename, or database reference such as /data/soil_ph/readout_001.csv.

soil_moisture_capture.reasoning: For the soil_moisture_capture Capture node, I included only instrument/session configuration fields needed to describe how soil moisture was measured in the field or lab. I excluded the moisture readout itself because that belongs on the downstream soil_moisture_signal node, and I excluded soil identity, collection context, and chemical/temperature descriptors because those belong to the upstream soil_sample Entity node or separate capture nodes. I also avoided any extraction, sequencing, or analysis fields because they are outside this node's semantic territory. No already_generated fields were provided, so I did not need to avoid prior overlaps. The schema focuses on the hardware, method, and session conditions that determine how the moisture measurement was acquired.

md_schema.descr: Manufacturer of the soil moisture probe used to measure volumetric or gravimetric moisture content during the capture session. Record the hardware brand name as a string, for example Campbell Scientific or Decagon Devices.
Model name or number of the soil moisture probe used for the measurement session. Record the exact instrument model as deployed in the field or laboratory, for example 5TE or ThetaProbe ML3.

Serial number of the moisture probe used in the capture session, recorded from the device label or instrument inventory. Use a stable string identifier such as SN00012345 to trace the exact hardware unit.

Operational method used to capture soil moisture at the time of measurement, such as in situ probe insertion, gravimetric estimation, or sensor-based volumetric reading. Choose the method actually used in this experiment.

Depth at which the moisture reading was acquired, measured in centimeters from the soil surface during the capture session. Typical values depend on the sampling design and may range from 0 to 100 cm.
Date on which the soil moisture measurement was performed, recorded at the capture session in YYYY-MM-DD format. Use this to distinguish repeated measurements across field visits.
Clock time when the soil moisture measurement was performed, recorded in 24-hour HH:MM format. Useful when multiple measurements are taken on the same day.
Person or field crew member who performed the soil moisture measurement. Record as a string identifier or name, for example technician_02, to document the measurement session.

Calibration status of the moisture probe immediately before or during the measurement session, indicating whether the device was verified against a standard or factory setting. Capture this at measurement time to support reproducibility.

soil_moisture_signal.reasoning: For the soil_moisture_signal Signal node, I included only raw data artefact fields that describe the moisture readout itself: the measured moisture value, its unit/basis, and simple technical quality/storage descriptors. I excluded probe manufacturer/model, calibration, and measurement depth because those belong to the upstream soil_moisture_capture node. I also excluded soil identity and collection context because those belong to the soil_sample Entity node. No already_generated fields were provided, so there were no existing-name conflicts to avoid. The resulting schema is limited to the recorded moisture signal and its technical representation so downstream users can archive and reuse the measurement without mixing in capture settings.

md_schema.descr: Recorded soil moisture readout for the sample, captured as the raw numeric signal from the moisture measurement session. Typical values depend on method and are often reported as volumetric water content or percent moisture.
Unit or reporting basis used for the moisture readout, such as percent, volumetric_fraction, or gravimetric_fraction. Record the exact basis used in the signal record.
Textual representation of the moisture signal as stored in the raw record or export table, such as 23.4 or 0.234. Useful when the original output is preserved as a string.
Quality flag for the recorded moisture readout indicating whether the signal was accepted, corrected, or rejected due to sensor or handling issues. Assign this when the raw readout is archived.

Storage location or file reference for the raw moisture readout if it is written to a digital log, spreadsheet, or database table. Use a path, filename, or database reference such as /data/soil_moisture/readout_001.csv.

soil_temp_capture.reasoning: For the soil_temp_capture Capture node, I included only instrument/session configuration fields describing how soil temperature was measured. I excluded the temperature readout itself because that belongs to the downstream soil_temp_signal node, and I excluded soil identity, site, and collection context because those belong to the upstream soil_sample Entity node. I also excluded extraction, sequencing, and analysis details because they are outside this node's semantic territory. No already_generated fields were provided in this turn, so there were no prior field-name conflicts to avoid. The schema focuses on the configured thermometer/sensor, measurement method, and session metadata needed to reproduce the capture.

md_schema.descr: Manufacturer of the field thermometer or temperature sensor used to measure soil temperature during the capture session. Record the hardware brand name as a string, for example Thermo Fisher Scientific or Testo.
Model name or number of the thermometer or temperature sensor used for the measurement session. Record the exact device model as deployed in the field, for example Testo 174T or HOBO UX100.

Serial number of the temperature sensor used in the capture session, recorded from the device label or instrument inventory. Use a stable string identifier such as SN9876543 to trace the exact hardware unit.
Operational method used to capture soil temperature at the time of measurement, such as probe insertion, surface contact, or in situ buried sensor. Choose the method actually used in this experiment.

Depth at which the temperature reading was acquired, measured in centimeters from the soil surface during the capture session. Typical field values may range from 0 to 100 cm depending on study design.
Date on which the soil temperature measurement was performed, recorded at the capture session in YYYY-MM-DD format. Use this to distinguish repeated measurements across field visits.
Clock time when the soil temperature measurement was performed, recorded in 24-hour HH:MM format. Useful when multiple measurements are taken on the same day.
Person or field crew member who performed the soil temperature measurement. Record as a string identifier or name, for example technician_03, to document the measurement session.

Calibration status of the temperature sensor immediately before or during the measurement session, indicating whether the device was verified against a standard or used in factory setting. Capture this at measurement time to support reproducibility.

soil_temp_signal.reasoning: For the soil_temp_signal Signal node, I included only raw data artefact fields describing the temperature readout itself: the numeric value, unit, storage representation, and a basic quality flag/location. I excluded thermometer manufacturer/model, calibration, depth, and session timing because those belong to the upstream soil_temp_capture node. I also excluded soil identity and site context because those belong to the soil_sample Entity node. No already_generated fields were provided in this turn, so there were no prior naming conflicts to manage. The schema is limited to the recorded temperature signal and its technical storage properties so downstream users can archive or reuse the measurement without mixing in capture settings.

md_schema.descr: Recorded soil temperature readout for the sample, captured as the raw numeric signal from the temperature measurement session. Typical values in agricultural soils may range from below 0 to above 40 degrees Celsius depending on season and depth.
Unit used for the temperature readout as stored in the raw record, typically degrees Celsius for this study. Record the exact unit basis associated with the signal value.
Textual representation of the temperature signal as stored in the raw record or export table, such as 18.6 or 294.95. Useful when the original output is preserved as a string.
Quality flag for the recorded temperature readout indicating whether the signal was accepted, corrected, or rejected due to sensor or handling issues. Assign this when the raw readout is archived.

Storage location or file reference for the raw temperature readout if it is written to a digital log, spreadsheet, or database table. Use a path, filename, or database reference such as /data/soil_temperature/readout_001.csv.

nucleic_acid_extraction.reasoning: For the nucleic_acid_extraction Process node, I included only protocol and reagent details that describe how community nucleic acids were extracted from the soil sample, plus a process-level quality indicator and the software is not relevant here. I excluded soil identity and collection context because those belong to the upstream soil_sample Entity node, and I excluded the extracted nucleic acids product properties because those belong to the downstream extracted_nucleic_acids Entity node. I also excluded library prep, sequencing, and analysis details because they are outside this node's semantic territory. No already_generated fields were provided in this turn, so there were no prior field-name conflicts to avoid. The schema focuses on the extraction method, reagents, and conditions needed to reproduce the process and assess extraction performance.

md_schema.descr: Primary extraction approach used to recover community nucleic acids from the soil sample, recorded at the time the process was performed. Examples include bead-beating plus chemical lysis or column-based extraction.
Commercial kit or extraction reagent system used for soil nucleic acid extraction, recorded as the exact product name if applicable. Example: DNeasy PowerSoil Kit.
Lot or batch number of the extraction kit or critical reagent set used during the process, recorded to support traceability of reagent performance. Use a string such as LOT12345.
Mass of soil input used for extraction, measured at the start of the process in grams. Typical values in soil metagenomics workflows are often between 0.1 and 10 g depending on protocol.
Duration of the lysis step used during nucleic acid extraction, measured in minutes from start to stop of the active disruption phase. Record the actual process duration used in this experiment.
Final elution volume used to recover the extracted nucleic acids, measured in microliters at the end of the extraction process. Typical volumes may range from 20 to 200 µL.

Process-level quality indicator for the extraction outcome, assigned after completion based on whether nucleic acids were recovered in usable quantity and integrity for downstream library preparation. Use this flag to summarize extraction success or failure.
Person or laboratory staff member who performed the nucleic acid extraction process. Record as a string identifier or name, for example technician_01, to document the operator responsible.

extracted_nucleic_acids.reasoning: For the extracted_nucleic_acids Entity node, I included intrinsic properties of the recovered nucleic acid material itself: its identity/linkage to the source sample, concentration, purity/integrity, and basic storage/origin attributes. I excluded extraction protocol details because those belong to the upstream nucleic_acid_extraction Process node, and I excluded library prep, sequencing, and downstream analytical fields because they belong to later nodes. I also avoided soil collection and environmental descriptors because those belong to the soil_sample Entity node and the separate capture/signals for pH, moisture, and temperature. No already_generated fields were provided in this turn, so there were no prior name conflicts to manage. The schema is centered on the material’s quantity and quality so downstream users can assess whether the extract was suitable for library preparation.

md_schema.descr: Unique identifier for the nucleic acid extract derived from a soil sample, used to track the purified material through library preparation and sequencing. Use a stable string such as EXTRACT_0001 or SAMPLE01_EXTRACTA.

Identifier of the upstream soil sample from which this nucleic acid material was obtained. Use the same sample identifier assigned at the entity level, for example SAMPLE_0001, to maintain provenance.

Measured concentration of the purified nucleic acid extract at the point it is made available for downstream library preparation, expressed in ng/µL. Typical values in soil metagenomics extracts may range from near 0 to several hundred ng/µL.

Total mass of nucleic acid recovered from the extraction, calculated or measured at the end of the extraction process in nanograms. This describes the amount of material available for sequencing preparation.

Spectrophotometric purity ratio of absorbance at 260 nm to 280 nm for the extracted nucleic acids, recorded after purification and before library preparation. Typical values for relatively pure DNA are around 1.7 to 2.0.

Spectrophotometric purity ratio of absorbance at 260 nm to 230 nm for the extracted nucleic acids, recorded after purification and before library preparation. Typical values for relatively clean extracts are often near 2.0.

Approximate dominant fragment size of the extracted nucleic acid material, measured after extraction and before library preparation, in base pairs when applicable. Use this field to describe the size distribution if assessed by electrophoresis or fragment analysis.

Storage condition for the extracted nucleic acids after purification and before downstream use, such as frozen, refrigerated, or lyophilized. Record the condition used to preserve the material between steps.

library_prep.reasoning: For the library_prep Process node, I included only protocol and reagent details that describe how extracted nucleic acids were converted into a sequencing-ready library, plus process-level settings and a preparation QC indicator. I excluded the source soil sample and extract identity because those belong to upstream Entity nodes, and I excluded the finished library's intrinsic properties because those belong to the downstream metagenomic_library Entity node. I also excluded sequencing instrument settings and raw read/file properties because those belong to later Capture/Signal nodes. No already_generated fields were provided in this turn, so there were no prior field-name conflicts to avoid. The schema centers on the library construction workflow details needed to reproduce the preparation and interpret whether the library was suitable for sequencing.

md_schema.descr: Primary library construction approach used to convert extracted nucleic acids into a sequencing-ready metagenomic library, recorded at the time the process was performed. Examples include tagmentation or ligation-based library preparation.
Commercial kit or reagent system used for library preparation, recorded as the exact product name if applicable. Example: Nextera DNA Flex or NEBNext Ultra II.
Lot or batch number of the library preparation kit or critical reagent set used during the process, recorded to support traceability of reagent performance. Use a string such as LOT67890.
Mass of extracted nucleic acid input used at the start of library preparation, measured in nanograms. Typical values depend on protocol and often range from sub-nanogram to hundreds of nanograms.

Method used to fragment nucleic acids during library preparation, if fragmentation was performed, such as enzymatic, mechanical, or tagmentation-mediated fragmentation. Record the actual method used in this experiment.

Number of PCR amplification cycles used during library preparation, counted during the amplification stage immediately after adapter addition or enrichment. Typical values are protocol-specific and often range from 0 to 20 cycles.
Final volume of the prepared library prior to sequencing, measured in microliters at the end of library preparation. Use this value to document the amount of library material available for loading.

Process-level quality indicator for the library preparation outcome, assigned after completion based on whether the library met size, concentration, and cleanliness requirements for sequencing. Use this flag to summarize preparation success or failure.
Person or laboratory staff member who performed the library preparation process. Record as a string identifier or name, for example technician_04, to document the operator responsible.

metagenomic_library.reasoning: For the metagenomic_library Entity node, I included intrinsic properties of the prepared library itself, such as its identity, linkage to the source extract, concentration, fragment-size characteristics, adapter/index composition, and storage status. I excluded library construction details because those belong to the upstream library_prep Process node, and I excluded sequencing instrument settings and raw-read file properties because those belong to the downstream metagenomic_sequencing Capture and raw_metagenomic_reads Signal nodes. I also avoided soil collection, extraction, and environmental descriptors because those are owned by earlier nodes in the DAG. No already_generated fields were provided in this turn, so there were no preexisting naming conflicts to avoid. The schema is aimed at the library’s composition and readiness so downstream users can understand what material was loaded into sequencing.

md_schema.descr: Unique identifier for the prepared metagenomic library, used to track the library through sequencing and downstream analysis. Use a stable string such as LIB_0001 or SAMPLE01_LIBA.
Identifier of the upstream nucleic acid extract from which this library was prepared. Use the extract identifier assigned at the entity level, for example EXTRACT_0001, to maintain provenance.

Measured concentration of the prepared sequencing library at the point it is made available for loading onto the sequencer, expressed in ng/µL. Typical values depend on the library system and may range from very low to several tens of ng/µL.

Approximate dominant fragment size of the prepared library, measured after library construction and before sequencing, in base pairs. Record the size distribution if assessed by electrophoresis or fragment analysis.
Adapter or index sequence associated with the library, used for sequencing and sample demultiplexing. Record the sequence or index identifier used for this prepared library.
Molar concentration of the prepared library, measured before sequencing loading and expressed in nM. Typical values are platform and protocol dependent and are used to normalize pooling.
Storage condition for the prepared library before sequencing, such as frozen, refrigerated, or immediate use. Record the condition used to preserve the library between preparation and capture.

Indicator of whether the prepared library met the requirements for sequencing loading at the time of handoff to the sequencing step. Use this to capture readiness status of the entity, not the preparation process outcome.

metagenomic_sequencing.reasoning: For the metagenomic_sequencing Capture node, I included only instrument/session configuration fields describing the sequencing run and the sequencer hardware because this node represents the measurement session and instrument settings. I excluded raw read file properties and quality metrics because those belong to the downstream raw_metagenomic_reads Signal node. I also excluded library identity and composition because those belong to the upstream metagenomic_library Entity node, and I excluded extraction/library-prep protocol details because those belong to earlier Process nodes. No already_generated fields were provided in this turn, so there were no prior naming conflicts to avoid. The schema focuses on the sequencer, run setup, and acquisition settings needed to reproduce the sequencing capture.

md_schema.descr: Manufacturer of the sequencing instrument used to read the metagenomic library during the capture session. Record the hardware brand name as a string, for example Illumina or Oxford Nanopore Technologies.
Model name or number of the sequencing instrument used for the capture session. Record the exact platform model, for example NovaSeq 6000 or MiSeq.

Serial number of the sequencing instrument used in the capture session, recorded from the instrument label or inventory record. Use a stable string identifier such as SN20240001 to trace the exact hardware unit.
Sequencing chemistry or kit version used during the run, recorded at the time of capture. Examples include SBS v3 or a platform-specific chemistry designation.
Operational sequencing run type used for the capture session, such as single-end, paired-end, or long-read mode. Record the actual run configuration used in this experiment.

Configured read length in base pairs for the sequencing run, measured or specified at run setup. Typical values depend on platform and may range from tens to several hundred base pairs for short-read sequencing.
Identifier of the sequencing lane, flow cell, or equivalent consumable used for the capture session. Use the exact run container identifier such as lane_1 or flowcell_ABC123.
Date on which the sequencing run was performed, recorded at the capture session in YYYY-MM-DD format. Use this to distinguish repeated sequencing runs on the same library.
Person or facility staff member who operated the sequencing run. Record as a string identifier or name, for example technician_05, to document the capture session operator.

raw_metagenomic_reads.reasoning: I corrected the raw_metagenomic_reads Signal schema by removing the collided field read_length_bp, since it had already been generated for an earlier DAG step. I kept only fields that still describe the raw sequencing artefact itself: file format, file size, read count, quality status, storage location, and demultiplexing state. I did not add upstream capture or library-preparation fields, and I avoided reusing any already_generated meaning. The revised schema stays within Signal territory and remains useful for locating, validating, and reusing the raw metagenomic read files.

md_schema.descr: File format of the raw metagenomic sequencing reads as stored after the sequencing run, such as FASTQ or BAM. Record the exact technical format used for the raw data artefact.

Total size of the raw read file or files associated with the sequencing output, measured in bytes at the time of storage or archival. Typical values may range from millions to billions of bytes depending on run depth.
Total number of raw sequencing reads generated for the library and stored in the raw data artefact. Record the exact count at the time the file is finalized or archived.

Technical quality flag for the raw sequencing reads indicating whether the file is complete, truncated, or otherwise suitable for downstream processing. Assign this when the raw data artefact is archived.
Storage location or file reference for the raw metagenomic reads, such as a path, filename, or object-store identifier. Example: /data/metagenomics/sample01_R1.fastq.gz.

Indicator of whether the raw read file has already been demultiplexed into sample-specific reads at the time it is stored. Use this to describe the state of the raw signal artefact, not the sequencing instrument.

read_processing.reasoning: For the read_processing Process node, I included only computational workflow details describing how raw reads were filtered and transformed into a community profile, plus the software agent metadata required by the rules. I excluded raw read file properties because those belong to the upstream raw_metagenomic_reads Signal node, and I excluded the resulting community profile/table properties because those belong to the downstream community_abundance_matrix Derivative node. I also excluded soil sample identity and environmental measurements because those are owned by earlier Entity/Capture/Signal nodes. Because read_length_bp was already used elsewhere in the DAG, I avoided it entirely and used other process-specific fields instead. The schema focuses on the processing algorithm, key thresholds, and output quality so downstream users can reproduce the computational step and judge its reliability.

md_schema.descr: Name of the software or workflow package used to process the raw metagenomic reads into a community profile. For this DAG, the processing agent is QIIME2, which should be recorded here as the software system used for the computation.
Version of the processing software used for the read-processing step, recorded at the time the computation was run. Example: v2024.10 or an equivalent release identifier.
Repository, package source, or project reference for the processing software used in this step, recorded to support reproducibility. Example: a GitHub URL or package registry identifier.

Primary computational filtering strategy applied to the raw reads during processing, recorded at the time the pipeline was run. Examples include quality trimming, host removal, chimera filtering, or denoising.

Minimum per-base quality score threshold used during read filtering, recorded for the computational process that generated the community profile. Typical short-read workflows use thresholds in the range of 10 to 30.

Minimum accepted read length in base pairs after filtering, used to retain reads for community profiling. Record the threshold applied in this processing step, typically platform- and protocol-specific.

Method used to summarize processed reads into a community profile, such as amplicon sequence variant inference, OTU clustering, or taxonomic aggregation. Record the actual computational summarization approach used in this experiment.

Process-level quality indicator summarizing whether the read-processing step completed successfully and yielded a usable community profile for downstream ecological analysis. Assign this at the end of the processing step.

community_abundance_matrix.reasoning: For the community_abundance_matrix Derivative node, I included only computed-result fields that describe the derived table itself: what algorithmic output it is, how it is dimensioned, what feature and abundance units it contains, and basic quality/completeness indicators. I excluded raw read properties and sequencing settings because those belong to upstream Signal/Capture nodes, and I excluded the read-processing software parameters because those belong to the upstream read_processing Process node. I also avoided the already-used field name read_length_bp and did not repeat any upstream sample or environmental descriptors. The schema is focused on the matrix as a computed artefact so downstream users can understand the structure and usability of the abundance table for ecological analyses.

md_schema.descr: Unique identifier for the derived community abundance matrix, used to track the computed table through downstream analysis. Use a stable string such as MATRIX_0001 or SAMPLE01_MATRIXA.
Identifier of the upstream read-processing step that generated this matrix. Use the processing node identifier, for example read_processing, to maintain provenance for the derived result.
Definition of the microbial features represented as rows or columns in the abundance matrix, recorded as the computational basis of the derived result. Examples include ASVs, OTUs, or taxa.

Number of features represented in the abundance matrix, measured after computation is complete. This is the total number of rows if features are rows, or the equivalent feature count in the final table.
Number of samples represented in the abundance matrix, measured after computation is complete. This is the total number of sample columns or equivalent dimensions in the derived table.
Unit or representation used for the abundance values in the matrix, recorded for the derived table. Common examples include relative abundance, counts, or normalized abundance.
Normalization or scaling method applied when generating the matrix, if any, recorded as part of the derived result. Examples include rarefaction, total-sum scaling, or no normalization.
Quality indicator describing whether the derived matrix is complete and suitable for downstream ecological analysis. Assign this after computation to reflect missingness or generation problems.
Storage location or file reference for the derived abundance matrix, such as a path, filename, or database identifier. Example: /results/community_abundance_matrix.tsv.

integrative_analysis.reasoning: For the integrative_analysis Process node, I included only analysis workflow details: the statistical/ecological approach, the software agent metadata required by the rules, and key model/design settings used to relate the community profile to soil pH, moisture, and temperature. I excluded the upstream signal values for pH, moisture, and temperature because those belong to their respective Signal nodes, and I excluded the community matrix properties because those belong to the upstream community_abundance_matrix Derivative node. I also excluded the final association result fields because those belong to the downstream community_association_results Derivative node. No already_generated fields were provided in this turn, so there were no prior field-name conflicts to avoid. The schema focuses on how the integrative analysis was performed and what statistical design was used to assess geographic and seasonal associations.

md_schema.descr: Name of the software or workflow package used for the integrative environmental association analysis. For this DAG, the processing agent is an R-based statistical ecology workflow, which should be recorded here as the software system used for the computation.
Version of the analysis software used for the integrative analysis step, recorded at the time the computation was run. Example: 4.4.0 or an equivalent release identifier.

Repository, package source, or project reference for the analysis software used in this step, recorded to support reproducibility. Example: a GitHub URL, CRAN package reference, or internal workflow repository identifier.

Primary statistical test or model family used to assess association between microbial community patterns and environmental variables, recorded at the time the analysis was run. Examples include linear models, mixed-effects models, PERMANOVA, or redundancy analysis.

List or short description of covariates included in the integrative model beyond soil pH, moisture, and temperature, recorded as part of the analysis design. Use a concise string such as season, site, or geographic_region.
Indicator of whether seasonal variation was explicitly tested in the integrative analysis model. Record this at analysis setup time to document the study design.
Indicator of whether geographic location or site effects were explicitly tested in the integrative analysis model. Record this at analysis setup time to document the study design.
Method used to adjust for multiple hypothesis testing in the integrative analysis, if applicable. Examples include Benjamini-Hochberg or Bonferroni correction.
Process-level quality indicator summarizing whether the integrative analysis completed successfully and produced interpretable association outputs. Assign this at the end of the analysis step.

community_association_results.reasoning: For the community_association_results Derivative node, I included only computed-result fields that describe the statistical outputs themselves: the result identifier, source analysis provenance, effect/p-value/FDR summaries, significance classification, and storage location. I excluded the underlying environmental measurements and community-matrix properties because those belong to upstream Signal and Derivative nodes, and I excluded analysis method settings because those belong to the upstream integrative_analysis Process node. I also avoided reusing any previously generated field names. The schema is focused on the final statistical artefact so downstream users can interpret, filter, and reuse the association results without conflating them with the analysis procedure that produced them.

md_schema.descr: Unique identifier for the derived association-results table or result set, used to track the statistical output through reporting and downstream interpretation. Use a stable string such as RESULTS_0001 or ANALYSIS01_RESULTS.
Identifier of the upstream integrative analysis step that generated these results. Use the analysis node identifier, for example integrative_analysis, to maintain provenance for the derived result.

Environmental or contextual variables tested against the microbial community patterns in the result set, recorded as a concise string or list representation. Examples include soil pH, moisture, temperature, season, and geographic location.

Primary effect size metric reported in the association results, such as beta coefficient, correlation coefficient, R-squared, or PERMANOVA pseudo-F depending on the analysis method. Record the metric actually used in the statistical output.
Nominal p-value threshold used to call statistical significance in the association results, recorded as part of the output interpretation. Typical thresholds include 0.05 or 0.01.

False discovery rate threshold used to classify significant associations after multiple testing correction, recorded as part of the derived result interpretation. Typical values are 0.05 or 0.1 when applicable.

High-level summary of which associations were significant in the derived output, recorded as a compact string or categorical summary. Use this to describe the overall result pattern rather than individual rows.
Storage location or file reference for the derived association results, such as a path, filename, or database identifier. Example: /results/community_association_results.tsv.
